title: The room that watches itself
topic: A Houston Methodist study of cameras in a cardiothoracic operating suite estimates about 25 more cases a month and its authors call the rise associated with the rollout, not caused by it

scenes.vo: In a cardiothoracic suite at Houston Methodist Hospital, four cameras on the walls of each operating room watched each case.
scenes.on_screen: A generic cardiothoracic operating room lights up around a surgical table as its four wall cameras lift their heads and scan on standby. A name plate reading cardiothoracic suite settles on the wall. The four wall cameras light one after another around the room, each lamp holding on. Gloved hands wheel a patient shape on a gurney up to the suite doorway as all four lit cameras turn to it.

requests.purpose: Give the film one generic cardiothoracic operating room with four wall cameras, a table, a clock ring and a surgeon phone, so the suite the study describes is a recognizable place that changes state through the film.
requests.prompt: Author an original finished React and SVG object in the current Remotion engine. A generic cardiothoracic operating room with cool tile, a surgical table with a patient shape and a drape with a lopsided fall, four rounded wall cameras with small amber status lamps that light in turn, a round room clock ring with no numerals and four event markers, and a surgeon phone held at the edge of the frame with a text alert. Cool overhead surgical light, a warm practical, soft contact shadows. No logos, no vendor interface, no real staff, no face. Maintained but worn, nothing symmetric. A disclosed illustration, never a real room.
requests.source_limit: Disclosed illustration of a generic suite. Not the Walter Tower room, not an Apella interface, and no second level timing or real staff or patient.

requests.purpose: Give the room its records: a study card, a suite line against a dashed comparison line, a cases counter, a percent badge, an interval whisker, a placebo stamp, an associated with the rollout card, a bundle band, a minority stake slice and a blank turnover box.
requests.prompt: Author an original finished React and SVG support group in the current Remotion engine. A study card with worn corners, a solid teal suite line against a dashed gray comparison line, a monthly cases counter, a seven percent badge, an interval whisker with end caps and a cases a month label, a row of comparison bars with a crooked stamp reading short of conventional significance, a card reading associated with the rollout not caused by it with a dashed link and a struck solid arrow, a camera tag bound to workflow review notes by a band, a minority slice of a ring with no number, and a dashed blank turnover box. Warm paper against cool gray steel. No logos, no brand marks, no page images.
requests.source_limit: Disclosed illustration of the study records. Every number is one the validated claims carry and none is invented.

event.note: second consolidated correction of the code review 2 blockers (attendant hand scale, drape pop-in, s10 layout)
one consolidated correction of the independent code review 1 defects

film_direction.angle: Follow the cardiothoracic suite from wall height, so the viewer sees the room keep its record before the study cards arrive as inserts.
film_direction.opening_promise: Watch four cameras light in a hospital suite, then see what the record does and does not show.
film_direction.performed_turn: The stamp lands crooked across the comparison bars and the solid caused arrow is struck through, so the number is shown as associated and not caused.
film_direction.closing_answer: A blank turnover box holds beside the room clock and the card of about 25 more cases a month joined to the rollout by its dashed associated link, the four camera lamps still lit, so the study does not show whether the rollout sped up turnover.

clauses.text: In a cardiothoracic suite at Houston Methodist Hospital,
four cameras on the walls of each operating room watched each case.
patient entry, draping and room turnover.
A hospital study compared that suite
and found about 25 more surgeries a month.
That is a rise of 7 percent.
runs from 8.3 to 41.0 cases a month.
A placebo test did not reach conventional significance.
The authors call the rise associated with the rollout,
The rollout came bundled with other workflow changes,
and the hospital holds a minority stake in the camera company.
The paper leaves turnover time for future work.
So the study does not show whether the rollout sped up room turnover.

story_contract.opening_question: Does a camera that logs an operating room add surgeries, or only count them?
story_contract.actor: Houston Methodist researchers, who published a study of cameras in a cardiothoracic operating suite
story_contract.action: Compared the camera suite with other Houston Methodist sites and estimated about 25 more cases a month.
story_contract.change: Operating room events such as patient entry, draping and turnover were timestamped from camera images, and surgeons were texted at draping.
story_contract.affected_people: Surgeons and operating room staff in the cardiothoracic suite. No person is named or drawn.
story_contract.consequence: The study estimates about 25 more cases a month that its authors call associated with the rollout, not caused by it.
story_contract.source_limit: Observational study with a bundled rollout, a placebo test short of conventional significance, hospital equity in the vendor and turnover time left for future work.
story_contract.closing_answer: The paper leaves turnover time for future work, so the study does not show whether the rollout sped up room turnover.

scenes.advances: A generic cardiothoracic operating room lights up around a surgical table as its four wall cameras lift their heads and scan on standby. A name plate reading cardiothoracic suite settles on the wall. The four wall cameras light one after another around the room, each lamp holding on. Gloved hands wheel a patient shape on a gurney up to the suite doorway as all four lit cameras turn to it.

The room clock ring draws itself on the wall beside the lit cameras. A camera pulse stamps a patient entry marker on the ring as the gurney carries the patient shape over the door threshold. A camera pulse stamps a draped marker on the ring as gloved hands open and lay the folded drape over the patient shape on the table. A camera pulse stamps a turnover marker on the ring as the draped patient leaves on the gurney and gloved hands lay a fresh sheet on the table.

A surgeon phone lights in a gloved hand while gloved hands wheel in the next patient shape and slide it onto the fresh sheet. Gloved hands open and lay the folded drape over the patient shape on the table. A text alert reading patient draped slides onto the phone.

A study card lands on the desk. The suite line and the dashed comparison line draw side by side across the card. The suite line climbs away from the dashed comparison line. A counter rises to about 25 more cases a month.

A 7 percent badge stamps beside the counter. The counter glows once under the badge. An empty axis labelled 95 percent confidence interval draws under the counter. An interval whisker draws outward from 8.3. The whisker reaches 41.0 and a label reading cases a month lands under it.

A row of ten gray placebo bars rises from the desk. The suite bar joins the row as the eleventh unit, every bar the same height. A stamp reading short of conventional significance lands crooked across the row.
A card reading associated with the rollout slides in beside the rollout tag. A dashed link draws from the rollout tag to the counter. A solid arrow marked caused draws once and is struck through.

The camera tag slides beside the stack of workflow review notes. A bundle band wraps the camera tag and the review notes together. A camera company tag and an empty ownership ring appear at the right. A minority slice of the ring lights on the camera company tag, with no number.
A paper card reading future work lands on the desk. The room clock ring draws beside the card with its turnover marker lit. The future work card tags the turnover marker.

A dashed blank box draws beside the turnover marker on the room clock. The turnover marker pulses once and the box stays blank. The room light lowers while the four camera lamps stay lit behind the blank box and the counter card.

creative_direction.visible_answer: The study finds about 25 more cases a month and can't say the cameras caused them, shown as a stamped comparison and a blank turnover box.
creative_direction.emotional_turn: Plain curiosity in the room, steady attention as the number arrives, a small doubt at the stamp, and then a level, open ending.
creative_direction.medium_choice: News report with explanatory animation, mechanism-led ordering. A static figure would show the event list but hide the room, the drape and the text the paper describes.

art_direction.palette_reason: A cool clinical gray-green carries the Houston operating room and its tile, steel and drape greens hold the table, warm paper carries the study cards, the pale shell gray of the cameras is the one clean value, and a single amber is kept for the lit camera lamps, the stamp and the text alert.
art_direction.shape_language: Rounded camera housings and a circular room clock against rectilinear tile, a crooked stamp, worn card corners and a drape with a lopsided fall. Nothing is symmetric.

lighting.motivation: Cool overhead surgical light with a warm practical from the desk lamp, a soft window light from the Houston side, and soft contact shadows to the right.

hero.silhouette: A compact room with four rounded wall cameras, a surgical table with a patient shape and drape, a round clock ring and a surgeon phone.
hero.finish: Cool lit tile and steel with a soft highlight on the camera housings, amber lamps, a drape with a lopsided fall, contact shadows under the table legs and a clean ring on the wall.

art_direction.focal_hierarchy: The cameras or the clock first, the markers or the counter second, the table and the cards third, the room and the window last.
art_direction.motion_language: Lamps tick on once, the clock ring draws at an even speed, markers and stamps land once, cards slide and settle without bounce, and the camera holds while objects perform.
